description:
Proposal page (approved 2026-11-07): https://claude.ai/artifact/Wx4cwENxiEe7qPfqni84ZN

A send runs the receiver's matcher on the sender against the sender's own message, copies only what the pattern binds (hit) or the message (miss) into a detached segment of the sender's own heap chain, and gifts that segment to the receiver through its in-queue under the receiver's queue lock. The receiver grafts the segment with pointer moves; the next Cheney pass treats it as from-space. No process ever writes into another process's live heap. Self-send is a mailbox push; the compiler's call-site publication of possibly-aliased arguments (construct_call_ownership) already keeps the message intact, so the runtime copies and publishes nothing.

Base: fz-sc8.66/scheduling-core @ 0163a8805 (PR #276). Work happens on one branch in worktree ../fz-gift and lands as one PR stacked on #276; each child ticket is one commit pushed to that PR as it closes.

Decisions taken from the proposal's open list: a gift's first block starts at the smallest size class and chains upward (measure before changing); tip adoption on graft is not built; the interpreter path is in scope for parity on every step.

Not in scope: multi-worker scheduling itself, receive markers, an off-heap message mode, the BEAM direct-on-heap try-lock fast path.
title: Gift-heap send: a sender matches in place and gifts a heap segment the receiver grafts
